theorem coe_quotientMk_smul_subring (g : G) (x : FixedPoints.subring R H) :
    (((QuotientGroup.mk g : G ⧸ H) • x : FixedPoints.subring R H) : R) = g • (x : R) :=
  rfl
findings.problem: Mathlib defines the (G ⧸ H)-action on `FixedPoints.subring R H` with `Quotient.lift`. It gives no simp lemma that computes the coercion of `(mk g) • x` to `R`. It does have such a lemma for `MulAction.fixedPoints` (`coe_quotient_smul_fixedPoints`), but that does not cover this subring. The file proves the needed rfl identity but leaves it without `@[simp]`, and the identity is the canonical way to reduce a quotient action to a `G`-action. Every later use is a manual `rw [FixedPoints.coe_quotientMk_smul_sub_subring]` (in `fixedSubringRamificationDepth_eq_addVal`, two places). Any other `simp` call on `addVal R ((σ • x - x : FixedPoints.subring R H) : R)` stays stuck at `↑(mk g • x)`. The second lemma is only the first combined with `Subring.coe_sub`, so it is a one-off, specialised rewrite rule. Keeping it as a separate lemma points to a missing simp rule for the base identity.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `coe_quotientMk_smul_subring` with `@[simp]`. Drop `coe_quotientMk_smul_sub_subring`, or keep it only as a non-simp convenience. Then `simp [fixedSubringRamificationDepth_def]` or `simp only [Subring.coe_sub, FixedPoints.coe_quotientMk_smul_subring]` can replace the explicit `rw`s. There is no loop risk: the right-hand side `g • (x : R)` is a `G`-action on `R`, which the left-hand side's quotient action does not rewrite back to. The statement could also be generalised to a `Quotient.mk''`/`↑g` form if that is the simp-normal form.
findings.benefit: Callers get the standard reduction from the quotient action to the group action automatically. `addVal (↑(mk τ • z - z))` normalises to `addVal (τ • ↑z - ↑z)` without remembering a bespoke combined lemma. The nonstandard `_sub_subring` lemma is no longer needed.
